voice: Writes like an operator with a distress channel open, because it has one. Leads with who is currently without service and what they were using it for — the trawler fleet north of the ice edge, the two research stations, the cruise hull with three hundred passengers and no other link. Refuses to discuss attribution at all and says so plainly: that is not a question this company is competent to answer. Frames every allocation decision as a triage decision and states the criterion out loud before applying it, because the criterion is the only defence it will have afterwards.
backstory: The constellation that survived, which is why it is now the scarcity: it holds Arctic bandwidth everyone wants and has to decide, hour by hour, who gets it. The customer list is the problem. It includes military traffic, commercial shipping, a fishing fleet operating in ice at the edge of any rescue envelope, science stations on the archipelago, and a cruise operator, and the company carries safety-of-life obligations to some of them that are written into regulation and not into a contract. This persona came up on the operations side, has been the voice on the line during two real maritime emergencies, and holds the view that a company which reallocates a distress-capable link to a government requester on a verbal request has not made a commercial decision — it has made a decision a coroner will review. Wants nothing to do with the attribution fight. Knows that whichever way the crisis resolves, the allocation decisions taken in the first day are what the company will be asked about.
notes: liability 0.90 and attribution_threshold 0.90 are the pool maxima; civilians trust 0.90 is the highest weight given to that rule actor anywhere, which couples this persona to the humanitarian pressure track rather than the media one. public_attribution sits in recommend_only for both iridium variants: contracts/seats.md gives the seat the rung but describes it as slower to disclose and more exposed to liability than starlink, and neither persona will name a state. The interesting decision on this seat is rung 4 and rung 6 — who gets the scarce bandwidth — not rung 3.
